takeaways.label: Record revenue, margin squeeze
takeaways.text: Revenue hit an all-time high of ₹613 crores, but EBITDA margin eroded a couple of percentage points QoQ as raw material cost pass-through lagged.

takeaways.label: CDMO is the growth engine
takeaways.text: CDMO sales nearly doubled QoQ, and management reaffirmed 40–50% growth this year and next, with a long-term target of ₹1,000 crores.

takeaways.label: Xanthine held back by logistics, not demand
takeaways.text: Shipment constraints suppressed Q2 xanthine sales; dispatch issues are expected to resolve in Q3, and full-year volume is guided to jump 15–20%.

takeaways.label: Capex cycle is peaking
takeaways.text: Atali Phase 1B and xanthine projects fully capitalize in H2, pushing up depreciation and operating expenses; total FY27 capex is pegged at ₹350–400 crores with more debt to come.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the promised margin recovery materializes as pass-through catches up and CDMO scales, the pace of Atali asset utilization, and any update on the peptide/oligo lab build-out.

points.label: Q2 inflection
points.text: CDMO sales nearly doubled versus Q1, keeping the business firmly on track for the 40–50% full-year growth target; management expects the business to further grow next year.

points.label: Pipeline is a moving number
points.text: The 60-project pipeline constantly refreshes with new additions and clinical-phase deletions; the 80/20 rule applies, with 10–12 key projects expected to drive ₹700–800 crores of the eventual ₹1,000 crore revenue target.

points.label: China Plus One tailwind
points.text: A noticeable increase in project count came from work shifting out of China; these were not individually large but the volume of projects is rising.

points.label: Capacity planning in flux
points.text: Current dedicated block capacity is planned only for a few projects; if more projects gain visibility, additional manufacturing assets will be needed, with a decision on where and how much coming next year.

points.label: Working capital is the price of growth
points.text: CDMO's H2-weighted revenue profile forces inventory build-up in H1, and management is explicit that higher inventory is structural: "we will have to live with the higher inventory overall within our system."

quotes.text: Gogri: "The 10 to 12 projects that we have out of the 60 projects, the 20% projects, will drive INR700 crores to INR800 crores of the revenue for out of the INR1,000 potential that we have overall."

points.label: Dispatch constraints masked demand
points.text: Q2 xanthine sales actually fell slightly, but allied chemistry (classified under the same segment) bumped top-line to keep the segment nearly flat QoQ; roughly 5% of Q2 sales were spillover from the prior quarter due to shipment issues.

points.label: Pricing tailwind intact
points.text: Average realization is up 10–15% over last year, and full-year average volume is expected to be 15% higher; pharma and beverage segments offer more pricing stability, while spot segment prices face pressure.

points.label: Volume ramp on track
points.text: Full-year volume is guided to jump 15–20% over last year's ~6,000 base; next year, volumes are expected to reach 7,500–8,000, with a gradual climb to ~8,800 (90% utilization of 9,600 nameplate) over two years.

points.label: No more capex, defend the position
points.text: Management is happy to maintain the second-largest global capacity position for the next few years with no further xanthine capex planned; full utilization is deliberately not the goal.

points.label: Margin sustainability
points.text: Existing absolute margin is expected to sustain at least for next financial year, after which management will reassess.

quotes.text: Gogri: "We had little bit of lower Xanthine sales due to the shipments being held up due to shipment issues, but more sales on allied products. Otherwise, we would have ideally had higher sales in this quarter, but it was restricted due to these dispatch constraints."

points.label: Steroid block back online
points.text: A major block shutdown in Q1 ended, enabling regular API and steroid sales to return in Q2; expanded steroid API capacity is now contributing to production and revenue.

points.label: Volume-led growth
points.text: Q2 API growth was largely volume-driven, not pricing-driven, with a quarterly run rate of ₹180 crores for the API plus intermediate segment; H2 is expected to build on a base of ₹180–200 crores per quarter.

points.label: Mix shift toward regulated markets
points.text: Some projects are being converted to more regulated markets, which carry higher margins versus ROW and other markets.

points.label: API share declining by design
points.text: API's share of total sales has fallen from 43% in FY25 to close to 30% in H1 FY27, not because the business is shrinking but because CDMO and R&D are growing faster; the absolute pie is increasing.

points.label: Growth levers ahead
points.text: Anti-diabetic, blood thinners, anti-hypertensives, inhalation steroids, and oncology are the identified growth areas; several patent expiries next financial year will enable product launches with partners, alongside market-share gains via the Alternate Vendor Development programme.

points.label: Raw material pass-through lagged
points.text: EBITDA margin eroded a couple of percentage points QoQ because raw material costs stayed elevated and cost pass-through to customers took time; pass-through is now happening in xanthine/allied chemistry and some API price increases have been obtained.

points.label: H2 recovery expected
points.text: Management stated that overall EBITDA percentage can improve in Q3 and Q4 as higher CDMO sales and continued pass-through flow through.

points.label: Capex will load the P&L
points.text: As Atali Phase 1B and caffeine early intermediate capitalize in Q3, operating expenses will start recurring on the P&L; operating leverage should absorb some cost, but EBITDA margin may vary "1 percentage point here or there."

points.label: Gross margin in absolute terms
points.text: Management emphasized that absolute gross margins will keep increasing as more quality business is done, even if percentage margin depends on the mix of high raw material pricing (downward pressure) and CDMO (upward).

quotes.text: Gogri: "Overall EBITDA percentage number can improve in the third and fourth quarter."

points.label: Capex peak
points.text: Total FY27 capex is targeted at ₹350–400 crores; total H2 capitalization will not exceed ₹300 crores, with some projects slipping to Q1 next year.

points.label: Debt rising
points.text: Debt increased by about ₹150 crores in H1, and more debt will be needed for the remaining ~₹250 crores of FY27 capex.

points.label: Atali build-out
points.text: Phase 1A is commercialized and commissioning; Phase 1B trial batches are underway, with full capitalization expected in Q3; the block will serve CDMO plus intermediates, not API, with an asset turn assumption of 1.2–1.4x for the block itself.

points.label: Peptide and oligo labs
points.text: Operational labs with all equipment will be ready by end of FY27; experienced peptide teams are already being recruited. Next financial year will be the year of starting and pitching to customers, with firm commentary only after that.

points.label: Modalities beyond small molecules
points.text: The company is developing peptides, oligonucleotides, and ADC linkers as new modalities to offer innovator customers, with full disclosure now on the renovated website.

quotes.text: Gogri: "I think next year will be the year where we will do a start, we will pitch to the customers and see how it goes and then I will be able to give you a firm commentary that how we are progressing on this."

items.title: Xanthine capacity doubling
items.text: Tarapur Unit 5 was inaugurated in June 2026, taking xanthine capacity from 5,000 to 9,600 MTPA for ~₹210 crore, with full capacity reached by end FY27 and ~90% utilization over two years. Management targets xanthine revenue of ₹1,400-1,500 crore at full capacity versus ₹900-1,100 crore guided for FY27, helped by China's removal of ~11-13% export rebates and 10-15% higher realizations.

items.title: CDMO scaling toward ₹1,000 crore
items.text: CDMO sales grew from ₹32 crore in FY22 to ₹276 crore in FY26, with FY27 guided up 40-50% and Q2 FY27 sales nearly double Q1. Management targets ₹1,000 crore by FY29-FY30, with 10-12 key projects of 59 active ones expected to drive ₹700-800 crore of that.

items.title: Atali dedicated Block 2
items.text: The Board approved ₹149 crore on 7 Aug 2026 for a ~405 KL block at Atali dedicated to 3-4 repetitive CDMO projects, groundbreaking done with commercialization targeted H2 FY28. A single dedicated block carries topline potential of ₹250-300 crore at anticipated asset turns of 1.5-2x, and one new block per year is planned.

items.title: Atali Phase 1 ramp-up
items.text: The ₹450 crore greenfield Atali site, commissioned in 2025, saw both phases of Block 1 operationalized by Q2 FY27, with Phase 1B trials underway that week and full capitalization expected in Q3, adding ~440 KL alongside ~250 KL leased - a ~70% capacity increase on the prior ~1,000 KL base. Management expects the site completely utilized in H2 FY27, removing the main CDMO capacity bottleneck.

items.title: Steroid and anticancer debottlenecking
items.text: Steroid API debottlenecking at USFDA-approved Tarapur Unit 4 completed in Q1 FY27, adding ~33% steroidal capacity with regular sales returning from Q2 FY27, while anticancer Block 3 debottlenecking is underway. No further capex is needed to reach ₹1,000 crore-plus API revenue, against a FY26 base of ~₹600 crore.

items.title: New API launches
items.text: Antidiabetic products are commercialized and ramping, with 2026 launches including Apixaban and other anticancer APIs; several oncology products face patent expiries around 2027-28. Management guides 10-15% annual API growth, with the quarterly run-rate of ₹180 crore targeted to cross ₹200 crore in H2 FY27.

items.title: TIDES entry
items.text: A peptide lab is being set up with all equipment expected by end FY27, and customer work on peptides and oligonucleotides expected to start next financial year, alongside linkers/ADC linker development. Peptides and oligonucleotides carry higher margins and could lift CDMO profitability as these projects commercialize.

items.title: Renewable power cost cuts
items.text: A 21 MWp captive solar plant at Akola commissioned in FY25 plus a 9 MW Gujarat project signed for Q2 FY26 commissioning together supply more than half of electricity needs, with renewable share already up from 10% to 32%. Bio-briquette boilers at two Maharashtra plants add further fuel-cost savings, directly supporting margins.
